title: withProjectionShards moves read-model indexing into N sharded workers that re-emit JOB_READ_READY to the host bus
content:
Projection shards scale the *read* path, where the worker pool scales the write path. Instead of the in-process read-model coordinator, the builder installs a shard manager that fans `JOB_WRITE_READY` events to N projection workers, sharded by document id. Each worker materializes the built-in read models against its own Postgres pool.

The part that makes it transparent to the rest of the reactor: each shard **re-emits `JOB_READ_READY` and the read-model events back to the host bus**, so synchronization, awaiters, and observers see them exactly once per job. Code that waits on `READ_READY` — including every `client.execute()` call — is unchanged by the topology.

```typescript
.withProjectionShards({
  db: { host: "localhost", port: 5432, database: "reactor", /* ... */ },
  shardCount: 4,
  preReadyKinds: ["document-view"],
  postReadyKinds: ["document-indexer"],
})
```

`preReadyKinds` run **before** a job reaches `READ_READY`; `postReadyKinds` run **after**. That split is the consistency dial: anything in `preReadyKinds` gates read-after-write and adds latency to every write, anything in `postReadyKinds` is eventually consistent but off the critical path. `BuiltInReadModelKind` is `"document-view" | "document-indexer"`.

Optional fields and their defaults: `poolSize` (overrides the reused worker DB pool size for shard pools only; `application_name` is forced to `"reactor-projection-shard"`), `initTimeoutMs` 30000, `shutdownGraceMs` 5000, `drainTimeoutMs` 30000, `chainDepthReportIntervalMs` 250.

Two build-time throws: `withProjectionShards` without a `db` anywhere gives `"withProjectionShards requires a db (or an executor worker pool configured with one); projection workers need connection info to open their own pools."`, and `shardCount < 1` gives `` `ProjectionShardManager: shardCount must be >= 1 (got ${shardCount})` ``. When the executor worker pool is also configured with a `db`, it may be omitted here and is reused.

Shards run standalone or alongside the worker pool — they replace the read-model coordinator, and the executor side is independent. Like the worker pool they require real Postgres, since the workers open their own pools and PGlite cannot cross threads.

Marked "not yet stable": the shard-manager class is internal, configured only through `withProjectionShards` and the public config types.

_Source: apps/academy/docs/academy/04-Reference/01-Reactor/07-StorageAndScaling.md (Powerhouse v6.2.2-dev.45)._
description: Shards fan JOB_WRITE_READY by document id, split work into preReadyKinds/postReadyKinds, and replace the in-process read-model coordinator. Requires Postgres.
